news.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
news.summary: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
news.summaryTr: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
news.articleText: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say - Published Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported, external. Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to recommend that under-25s are no longer able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip). Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. But many claimants would receive less under the plans, which the government is set to take forward into legislation in the new year. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Speaking to the Times about his report, Milburn said: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets, data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare reform under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch," Milburn added. He said that currently "you've got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job". His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, where young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. "A deal isn't a deal unless there are potential consequences," Milburn said. "Entitlements and responsibilities are two sides of the same coin." A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work. "But the prime minister has been clear that we need a wholesale change in the way we support young people to grow up in this country, where we invest in their success rather than paying for failure." news.title: Suiet wallet to shut down in latest exit from Sui ecosystem
news.summary: The self-custodial wallet will keep its API services running through Nov. 14. Sui’s DeFi total value locked has fallen more than 22% over the past month.

news.titleTr: Suiet wallet to shut down in latest exit from Sui ecosystem
news.summaryTr: The self-custodial wallet will keep its API services running through Nov. 14. Sui’s DeFi total value locked has fallen more than 22% over the past month.
news.articleText: Suiet wallet to shut down in latest exit from Sui ecosystem The self-custodial wallet will keep its API services running through Nov. 14. Sui’s DeFi total value locked has fallen more than 22% over the past month. Cryptocurrency wallet Suiet is shutting down, adding to a series of closures and service withdrawals in the Sui ecosystem. Suiet, a self-custodial wallet built for the Sui blockchain, said in a notice that it will stop updating and supporting its wallet, with API services set to end after Nov. 14. The shutdown comes as the Sui network has seen a sharp decline in decentralized finance (DeFi) activity. Sui’s total value locked (TVL) stood at about $413 million on Wednesday, down more than 22% over the past month, according to DefiLlama data. Data from Token Terminal shows that Sui averaged about 128,000 daily active users in October, down from 601,000 in November 2025 – or around a 79% drop. Meanwhile, other recent closures have also raised concerns about the costs and challenges of keeping projects running on the Sui network. “Sui’s problems seem to mostly be of an economic nature resulting from expensive engineering costs and low user volume rather than protocol failures,” Kadan Stadelmann, former chief technology officer of Komodo Platform, told Cointelegraph. “No flaw in the system’s core design has been found.” Cointelegraph reached out to the Sui Foundation and Suiet for comment but had not received responses by publication. Related: Sui DeFi protocol Full Sail to wind down after Switchboard incident Recent closures and departures Suiet’s shutdown immediately follows the Sui-based hardware wallet project Suiball also announcing its closure on Nov. 10. Meanwhile wallet provider Phantom ended support for Sui in September. DeFi project Full Sail also shut down following a security incident involving Switchboard that caused about $91,000 in losses. Despite the decline in active users, transactions on Sui have increased, reaching 324 million in October, up from 101 million in November 2025, according to Token Terminal. However, more transactions do not necessarily mean more users, and wallet providers must still decide whether supporting the network is worth the cost, according to Stadelmann. “Multi-chain wallets have expansive attack surfaces, and Sui’s approach adds costs for vendors who can take their business to less capital intensive chains,” he said. “Any individual failure of a multi-chain wallet is more a reflection of the risks rather than an indictment of any given protocol.” A series of outages Sui has also experienced four network outages in 2026, resulting in around 22 hours of combined downtime, according to reports published by the Sui Foundation. The network stopped processing transactions for about six hours in January, followed by three more outages on May 28 and 29. The May disruptions were linked to software bugs, including problems introduced by a network update, the Sui Foundation said at the time. By comparison, rival blockchain Solana has not recorded a network-wide outage since February 2024, when it went offline for nearly five hours. Meanwhile, Aptos, which uses the same underlying smart contract programming language as Sui, last reported a mainnet outage in October 2023. Network outages are significant because they can prevent DeFi users from trading, transferring funds or managing positions, although the Sui Foundation said no user funds were at risk during its May disruptions. news.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after affairs: WSJ
news.summary: The report about Huang’s possible departure came after the New York Times reported that he had a second extramarital affair.

news.titleTr: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after affairs: WSJ
news.summaryTr: The report about Huang’s possible departure came after the New York Times reported that he had a second extramarital affair.
news.articleText: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after affairs: WSJ The report about Huang’s possible departure came after the New York Times reported that he had a second extramarital affair. Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, The Wall Street Journal reported. Directors could meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. His potential removal would mark a major leadership change for the chipmaker, which has become central to the artificial intelligence boom under Huang. Cointelegraph reached out to Nvidia for comment but did not receive an immediate response. One affair involved Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer. US intelligence officials believe she was a spy for Beijing. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an extramarital affair with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, according to five people who worked at the company. On Sunday, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a letter to employees, apologizing for breaching their trust. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he wrote. Huang also confirmed that Nvidia’s board had launched an independent investigation into national security concerns raised in news reports. He pledged to cooperate fully and said he remained committed to the company. Nvidia shares fell 8% to $159.76 in after-hours trading following the reports, reversing a 2.9% gain during the regular session, according to Google Finance data. Yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın görevine devam edip etmeyeceğine ilişkin karar vermek üzere bir araya gelmesinin beklendiği belirtildi. Nvidia'dan henüz açıklama gelmedi Nvidia, Reuters'ın konuya ilişkin yorum talebine hemen yanıt vermedi. Gün içinde New York Times da Huang'ın doğrudan kendisine bağlı çalışan bir şirket yöneticisiyle evlilik dışı ilişki yaşadığını öne sürmüştü. Böylece Nvidia CEO'su hakkında aynı gün içinde iki ayrı ilişki iddiası gündeme geldi. Yönetim kurulu yabancı istihbarat iddiasını araştırıyor Gelişmeler, Huang'ın eşine sadık kalmadığını kabul etmesinden ve Nvidia yönetim kurulunun, CEO'nun yabancı bir istihbarat operasyonunun hedefi olup olmadığını araştırmaya başlamasından günler sonra yaşandı. Şirket yönetiminin yürüttüğü incelemenin, Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu şüphesi bulunan bir kadınla ilişki iddiasını da kapsadığı bildirildi. Nvidia hisselerinde sert düşüş Huang hakkındaki haberlerin ardından Nvidia hisseleri borsa kapanışı sonrasındaki işlemlerde yaklaşık yüzde 8 değer kaybetti. Şirket yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın geleceğine ilişkin nasıl bir karar alacağı ise belirsizliğini koruyor.

news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, OKX and Intercontinental Exchange are preparing to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23 despite objections from major companies, Barclays increased its holdings in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF by 48% in the third quarter, and pro-crypto lawmaker Tom Emmer was elected House Republican minority whip as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress. OKXICE moves ahead with tokenized stocks as blue chips push back Crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) are set to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23, despite objections from 67 companies to having their shares listed and warnings from Nasdaq that trading across disconnected platforms could fragment liquidity. The venture, known as OKXICE, will operate under the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s temporary Innovation Exemption and offer eligible US customers round-the-clock trading. Under the exemption, venues must give companies a chance to object before listing shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. JPMorgan Chase, McDonald’s, SpaceX and Coca-Cola were among the companies that objected. Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based tokens that represent company shares or track their price. The rights they carry depend on how they are structured. The distributed value of tokenized stocks and ETFs reached $3.88 billion on Nov. 11, up 13.4% over 30 days. In comments to Cointelegraph, former New York governor and OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo said investors would have “the same rights, protections and ownership that come with the underlying shares.” Barclays boosts BlackRock Bitcoin ETF stake 48% as banks expand holdings Barclays reported holding 3.94 million shares in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter, up 48% from the previous quarter. The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing. “Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup. Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). Its reported IBIT holdings also rose 50% to about 521,000 shares, from 347,000 at the end of June. The filings offer an early indication of changing institutional Bitcoin ETF ownership, with more major banks and hedge funds yet to disclose their third-quarter positions. Institutional investment managers have until Monday to file their third-quarter holdings reports. Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip Pro-crypto US Representative Tom Emmer has been elected House Republican minority whip, securing the party’s second-highest leadership position as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Emmer beat Texas Representative August Pfluger in a 103-76 secret ballot vote, according to Politico. He previously served as House Republican majority whip and will remain the party’s No. 2 leader, this time under incoming Minority Leader Jim Jordan. As minority whip, Emmer will be responsible for rallying Republican votes, coordinating the party’s legislative strategy and helping maintain unity on key bills. “Tom has been one of the strongest advocates for digital assets in Congress, and he has led the fight against a government-controlled CBDC and stood up for American innovators,” GOP Senator Cynthia Lummis said on X.

news.titleTr: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
news.summaryTr: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
news.articleText: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike - Published Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city. Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store. The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there." She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said. Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices. "We've completely brought the city to a standstill," a protester in Madrid told Reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. "Everyone's out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone's out on the streets." Another protester, 37-year-old teacher Olga Domingo, said she was protesting because "the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable". The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later. Rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 ($1,300; £1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460. That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform. Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes. And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing. "Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes. The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election. Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: "What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike." Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid. Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights. The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC. Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment. He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills. "It's absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas." He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible." With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible". However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing. "This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said. Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election. Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector. Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%. news.title: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress
news.summary: The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach.

news.titleTr: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress
news.summaryTr: The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach.
news.articleText: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach. Just over a week after a “blue wave” handed Democrats control of the US House and Senate, 14 races have yet to be called. The results so far have added crypto supporters in both chambers and the remaining races could bring more into Congress. Three candidates in the uncalled races received backing from crypto political action committees (PACs). According to Stand With Crypto, every candidate in those races is either strongly pro-crypto or has no stated position. As crypto advocacy groups look ahead to 2028, they’re turning their attention to candidates who have yet to take a public stance on crypto. House races still to be called Crypto PACs backed three candidates in US House races that remain undecided. Two incumbents lead in Alaska and North Carolina, while a Louisiana state senator faces a December runoff. Rep. Nick Begich leads in Alaska’s US House race. Defend American Jobs, Fairshake’s Republican-facing affiliate, backed him with $508,142 in the August primary. The same PAC put $150,600 behind Rep. David Rouzer, who leads in North Carolina’s 7th District. Louisiana state Sen. Blake Miguez will face Democrat Chauna Banks in a Dec. 12 runoff for the state’s 6th District. The Fellowship PAC backed Miguez with $250,000. The Associated Press called the race in South Carolina’s 2nd District for incumbent Rep. Joe Wilson on the morning of Nov. 11. Stand With Crypto rates Wilson as “strongly supportive of crypto.” His win brought the group’s House tally to 246 crypto supporters and 107 opponents, while the Senate stood at 50 supporters and 33 opponents. In the remaining races, Stand With Crypto lists each candidate as either strongly supportive of crypto or having no stated position. “The new members that have no stance present an opportunity,” Blockchain Association Chief Policy Officer Lindsay Fraser told Cointelegraph. Educating the incoming congress Nearly one in four members of the incoming Congress will be new, Fraser said, and many have given little thought to blockchain technology. “To us, that represents a blank slate in terms of education,” she said. Blockchain Association is planning a January fly-in to reach newly elected lawmakers. “Leaving the 120th Congress with more members in that A and B category would be a huge success,” she said, referring to Stand With Crypto’s ratings. The group gives an A to candidates who strongly support crypto and a B to those who are somewhat supportive. Fraser said age plays a bigger role than party affiliation in how lawmakers vote on crypto. She said members under 55 are much more likely to support the industry and that the incoming class skews younger. Fraser said she wants the industry to enter the 2028 election “with two candidates who […] are thoughtful in regards to the industry,” so the sector can avoid “living and dying by the outcome of that election.” Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

news.summary: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.

news.titleTr: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
news.summaryTr: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.
news.articleText: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms - Published Some Labour MPs have called on the government to reject the Rosebank oil field, saying it is "incompatible" with the UK's climate commitments. There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field off the north-west coast of Shetland will be given the go-ahead. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that a decision would be "taken in due course" while Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh stressed that affordability of energy bills was her "overriding objective". But in a sign of the division within the party, more than a dozen Labour MPs expressed concerns in Parliament about approving it. Others expressed support, pointing to economic benefits. Supportive Labour MPs said some other parts of the world emitted far more greenhouse gases than the UK and warned of relying on imports. Reports have suggested that Chancellor John Healey is in favour of approval. Separately, it is understood some Labour backbenchers have organised a letter opposing Rosebank - intended for Burnham, but not yet sent - which more than 60 out of about 400 Labour MPs have indicated they support. One signatory told the BBC that approving Rosebank "would not create new jobs, would bring minimal money into the Treasury and be bad for the climate". "The government's central aim is to tackle the cost of living crisis, and drilling for more oil at Rosebank isn't the answer," the MP said. Wednesday's Westminster Hall - a type of parliamentary debate where backbench MPs raise topical issues but do not vote - was organised by Green MP Carla Denyer. Labour MP for Sheffield Central Abtisam Mohamed told the debate: "Rosebank fails on every test. "It will not benefit taxpayers who will shoulder the vast majority of the development costs, it will not strengthen our energy security because most of the oil will be sold on international markets, and it will not reduce energy bills for our constituents, who will remain exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices." Richard Burgon, a former frontbencher on the left of the party, said: "Rosebank is not compatible with our climate targets - it's dangerous to pretend otherwise." The UK is committed to reaching net zero by 2050 and wants to limit global warming to no more than 1.5C above the pre-industrial period. The UK government has always insisted that Rosebank is a quasi-judicial decision, formally resting with Fahnbulleh. She green-lit production in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea last month, but Rosebank hangs in the balance. Labour's manifesto upon entering power in 2024 pledged not to "issue new licences to explore new fields". Licences for both Jackdaw and Rosebank were granted by the then Conservative UK government in 2022 and 2023 respectively. But the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that the government had made the approvals unlawfully, leaving the current Labour government to make a fresh decision on whether to give the go-ahead. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch sought to tease at Labour divisions on the issue during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday. Demand for fossil fuels During the debate, Labour MP Anna Gelderd said: "We live in an unprecedented era where our energy security is more vital than ever, in which jobs and wealth must be protected and economic opportunities seized - on both of these points, Rosebank fails." news.summaryTr: The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations.
news.articleText: Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital: Bloomberg The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations. Japanese financial services giant Nomura Holdings is reportedly weighing a sale of its cryptocurrency subsidiary Laser Digital as Nomura’s European operations continue to post losses. Nomura has held talks with potential buyers, including Marex Group, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. The company has yet to make a final decision and could keep the business, according to the report. Nomura’s European businesses posted a pretax loss of 7.4 billion yen ($46.5 million) in the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, their fourth consecutive quarterly loss. The company posted pretax profits in every other reporting region over the same period. Nomura did not disclose whether Laser Digital, which is headquartered in Switzerland, contributed to the European result. Nomura is one of Japan’s largest financial services groups, with its investment management division overseeing 152.8 trillion yen ($960 billion) in assets as of September 2026. The potential sale comes less than three months after Laser Digital Japan secured the country’s first new crypto exchange license in four years, allowing the firm to expand its institutional crypto trading services in Japan. Established in 2022, Laser Digital provides institutional cryptocurrency trading, asset management and venture investment services. The company has also pursued expansion in the United States, receiving preliminary approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for its proposed national trust bank in May. During a January earnings call, chief financial officer Hiroyuki Moriuchi said the company would reduce its cryptocurrency trading positions to limit short-term volatility while continuing to expand Laser Digital over the medium to long term. news.title: US data center restrictions could give Bitcoin miners an edge in AI, though challenges remain
news.summary: As US voters push back against new data centers, Bitcoin miners already expanding into AI could benefit from their existing facilities.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: US data center restrictions could give Bitcoin miners an edge in AI, though challenges remain
news.summaryTr: As US voters push back against new data centers, Bitcoin miners already expanding into AI could benefit from their existing facilities.
news.articleText: US data center restrictions could give Bitcoin miners an edge in AI, though challenges remain As US voters push back against new data centers, Bitcoin miners already expanding into AI could benefit from their existing facilities. Bitcoin miners with power already secured could have an edge in the race to build AI data centers after voters in several US communities backed limits on new development. The midterms could also bring closer scrutiny from Congress over who pays for the grid upgrades those facilities need, industry experts told Cointelegraph. Voters in several states weighed in on data center development during the Nov. 3 US midterms, when local measures appeared on the same ballots as congressional races. Amid concerns about rising electricity costs, water use and the impact on nearby communities, voters favored limiting development in 40 of the 41 local contests tracked by Ballotpedia. The restrictions include citywide bans, limits on larger facilities, temporary pauses on new projects and voter approval requirements for some developments. The results come as major Bitcoin mining companies continue moving into AI, a transition Jamie Brown, CEO of Global Kiwi Labs, said could become more attractive as local restrictions make it harder to build new data centers. “If a Bitcoin miner has not yet repurposed their electric contract and physical plant to AI, the case to do so just got more compelling,” said Brown, whose company hosts servers for crypto exchanges and trading firms. Related: US midterm elections 2026 as it happened: Democrats win control of Congress Local restrictions make expansion harder Miners’ shift to AI infrastructure is already underway, with publicly listed Bitcoin miners announcing more than $70 billion in AI and advanced computing contracts during 2025 and early 2026, according to a first-quarter report by CoinShares. But state and local decisions can have a more immediate impact on whether data center projects move forward. That’s because local authorities often oversee zoning and building permits and can influence access to electricity. “A company might have access to an attractive site and a significant amount of power capacity, but if local restrictions prevent it from expanding or upgrading that infrastructure, the opportunity becomes much more difficult to pursue,” said Jordan Knecht, head of strategic integrations at Kresus, a blockchain infrastructure company. Last week, voters backed 27 measures to limit or oppose new data centers in the elections, according to Ballotpedia. These included five complete bans, 12 partial bans and six-month pauses on new projects in three Maine towns. In Grove City, Ohio, voters approved a rule requiring public approval for large projects that use more than 20 megawatts of electricity, among other conditions. “Federal policy will certainly influence the broader investment environment, but the practical ability to develop and operate these facilities often comes down to conditions in individual markets,” Knecht told Cointelegraph. “For miners looking to transition into AI, I think understanding those local dynamics will be just as important as following developments in Washington.” Expanding into AI is not that simple Building AI-ready data center infrastructure can cost between $8 million and $15 million per megawatt, compared with $700,000 to $1 million per megawatt for traditional mining facilities, according to a 2026 report by CoinShares. That gap helps explain why a site with power already secured is only a starting point for miners moving into AI. “Transitioning from Bitcoin mining to AI workloads requires significant additional investment in infrastructure for cooling, networking, and reliability,” Knecht said. Yuliya Barabash, founder of SBSB Fintech Lawyers, also pointed to differences in electricity needs between Bitcoin mining and AI data centers. Bitcoin miners can often reduce electricity use when prices rise, while AI data centers typically need a consistent power supply, she said. “Higher electricity prices and additional regulatory requirements could make some projects less profitable or delay their implementation,” Barabash told Cointelegraph. This comes as electricity demand from US data centers is also expected to rise, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). The agency estimates that data centers used 224 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, a figure projected to nearly double to 426 terawatt-hours by 2030. The impact of Congressional changes One question facing the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress is who should pay to expand the grid for large data centers. Knecht said lawmakers could take a closer look at how those projects affect electricity costs and how they get approved. “There may be more pressure to ensure that large data center operators are paying their fair share of infrastructure costs rather than passing those expenses on to consumers.” Barabash also expects scrutiny of who pays for the electricity infrastructure needed to support data centers. “One of the key priorities is likely to be ensuring that technology companies, rather than ordinary consumers, bear the costs of the additional electricity infrastructure their facilities require,” she said. Still, experts noted that closer attention does not necessarily mean Congress will discourage data center development. “AI infrastructure is becoming increasingly important to the US economy, and there is still a strong incentive to support investment in domestic computing capacity,” Knecht said. For miners weighing a conversion, the question is whether AI revenue can justify the cost of upgrading cooling, networking and power systems. Brown thinks it can. “Miners will swap to AI because it is a better ROI than mining,” he said. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Afrika'da salgınının bilançosu ağırlaşıyor: 11 bin vaka, 5 bin ölüm - Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti’nde altı aydır devam eden Ebola salgınında vaka sayısı 11 bini, can kaybı 5 bini aştı. Sınır Tanımayan Doktorlar, salgının kontrol altına alınamadığını belirterek uluslararası topluma acil müdahale çağrısında bulundu. Sınır Tanımayan Doktorlar (MSF), Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti’nde (KDC) altı aydır devam eden Ebola salgınında vaka sayısının 11 bini, can kaybının ise 5 bini aştığını açıkladı. Salgının kontrol altına alınamadığını belirten MSF, uluslararası topluma acil müdahale çağrısında bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle MSF’nin yayımladığı raporda, ülke tarihinin en büyük ikinci Ebola salgınıyla mücadele için yüz milyonlarca dolarlık kaynak sağlanmasına rağmen sahadaki kritik eksikliklerin sürdüğü vurgulandı. Sağlık çalışanlarının yeterli ekipman ve desteğe ulaşamadığı, bazı bölgelerde ise salgın takibinin yetersiz kaldığı belirtildi. Ölümlerin üçte ikisi tedavi merkezleri dışında Raporda, geçen ay Ebola nedeniyle hayatını kaybedenlerin yaklaşık üçte ikisinin tedavi merkezleri dışında yaşamını yitirdiğine dikkat çekildi. MSF Uluslararası Başkanı Javid Abdelmoneim, salgınla mücadele için sağlanan büyük miktardaki fonlara rağmen sahadaki birçok görevlinin yeterli destekten yoksun olduğunu belirterek, "Bu durum kesinlikle kabul edilemez" dedi. Abdelmoneim, Ituri eyaletinde MSF tarafından tedavi edilen Ebola hastalarının yalnızca yüzde 9’unun daha önce temaslı olarak tespit edildiğini açıkladı. MSF, salgının yayılmasını önlemek için sağlık çalışanlarının desteklenmesi, vaka takip sisteminin güçlendirilmesi ve kaynakların en çok ihtiyaç duyulan bölgelere yönlendirilmesi çağrısında bulundu.

items.articleText: Dolarda korkutan fiyatlama: Son 1,5 yılın zirvesine tırmandı - ABD'de enflasyonun beklentileri aşması ve Fed yetkililerinin daha büyük faiz artışlarına kapıyı açık bırakması doları destekledi. Dolar endeksi yüzde 0,15 yükselerek 103,02'ye çıktı ve Nisan 2025'ten bu yana en yüksek seviyesini gördü. Japon yeni ise dolar karşısında 160 seviyesine yaklaştı. ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) faiz artırımlarına devam edeceği beklentisinin güçlenmesi, doları başlıca para birimleri karşısında 19 ayın zirvesine taşıdı. Japon yeninin dolar karşısında değer kaybetmesiyle dolar/yen paritesi de kritik 160 seviyesine yaklaştı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Reuters'ta yer alan habere göre, ABD'de ekim ayı enflasyonunun beklentilerin üzerinde gerçekleşmesi ve Fed yetkililerinin enflasyondaki katılığın devam etmesine ilişkin endişelerini dile getirmesi, yatırımcıların daha fazla para politikası sıkılaştırması beklentisini güçlendirdi. Yetkililerin 50 baz puanlık daha büyük bir faiz artışı ihtimalini de dışlamaması, doların yükselişini destekledi. Goldman Sachs'ın da aralarında bulunduğu bazı büyük aracı kurumlar, aralık ayında beklenen faiz artışının ardından gelecek yılın başlarında bir artış daha yapılacağını öngörüyor. Doların altı büyük para birimi karşısındaki değerini ölçen dolar endeksi, yüzde 0,15 artışla 103,02'ye yükseldi. Böylece endeks, Nisan 2025'ten bu yana en yüksek seviyesine ulaştı. Diğer başlıca para birimlerinde ise euro yüzde 0,06 değer kazanarak 1,1096 dolara yükselirken, sterlin yüzde 0,1 düşüşle 1,3266 dolara geriledi. National Australia Bank Kıdemli Piyasa Stratejisti Gavin Friend, New York Fed Başkanı John Williams'ın perşembe günü geç saatlerde katılacağı panelin piyasalar tarafından yakından izleneceğini belirtti. Friend, Williams'ın ekim ayındaki Federal Açık Piyasa Komitesi (FOMC) toplantısı öncesinde Fed'in faiz artırımları için zamanı bulunduğu yönündeki görüşlerini dile getirdiğini hatırlattı. Friend, ekim ayı Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE) verisinin beklentileri aşmasının ardından Fed yetkililerinin faiz artışlarını savunma konusunda yoğun bir tutum sergilediğini belirterek, Williams'tan gelecek mesajların piyasalar açısından önem taşıyacağını ifade etti. Yen 160 seviyesine yaklaştı Dolar, Japon yeni karşısında önceki kayıplarını geri alarak yüzde 0,04 artışla 159,83 seviyesinde işlem gördü. Yükselişte, Fed'in faiz artırımlarına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesi ve ABD ile Japonya arasındaki faiz farkının genişliği etkili oldu. Dolar/yen paritesi, perşembe günü erken saatlerde iki ayı aşkın sürenin en yüksek seviyesine çıkmıştı. Japonya Merkez Bankası (BOJ) yönetim kurulu üyesi Toichiro Asada'nın açıklamaları, yen üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı. Eylül ayında politika faizinin yüzde 1,25'e yükseltilmesine karşı çıkan iki güvercin üyeden biri olan Asada, yönetim kurulu içindeki kısa vadede faiz artırımı yapılması yönündeki çağrılara karşı çıktı. Asada, erken faiz artışlarının ekonomik büyümeyi olumsuz etkileyebileceğini ve enflasyonu aşağı çekebileceğini söyledi. Japonya'nın en üst düzey para birimi yetkilisi Atsushi Mimura'nın müdahale uyarısı ise dolar/yen paritesini gün içindeki en düşük seviyesine çekti. Mimura, Japon yetkililerin yaz aylarında gerçekleştirdiği döviz müdahalesinin unutulması için henüz erken olduğunu belirtti. Ancak yendeki toparlanma kısa sürdü. Matsui Securities Piyasa Analisti Sho Suzuki, dolar/yen paritesinin 160 seviyesini aşması durumunda piyasalardaki temkinliliğin daha da artacağını söyledi. Suzuki, doların mevcut seviyelerden daha fazla yükselmesi için Fed'in faiz artırımı beklentilerinin daha da güçlenmesi veya BOJ'un faiz artırımı beklentilerinin zayıflaması gibi dolar lehine yeni gelişmelere ihtiyaç olduğunu belirtti. Bu tür gelişmeler yaşanmadığı takdirde paritenin 160 seviyesinin üzerinde kalıcı bir kırılma gerçekleştirecek yeterli momentumu bulamayabileceğini ifade etti. Reuters anketine katılan çok sayıda analist, BOJ'un bir sonraki faiz artırımını aralık ayında gerçekleştirmesini bekliyor. Japonya'da perşembe günü açıklanan veriler de bu beklentileri destekledi. Ülkede yıllık toptan eşya enflasyonu ekim ayında yüzde 7,1'e yükselerek eylül ayındaki yüzde 6,8'lik seviyeyi aştı.

items.titleTr: New York building collapse kills at least two, officials say
items.summaryTr: A dangerous search for survivors continues after a three-storey building collapsed in Brooklyn on Wednesday afternoon.
items.articleText: New York building collapse kills at least two, officials say - Published At least two people have died and more than 17 others are injured after a building in New York City collapsed into an open construction site, officials have said. It sparked a massive search-and-rescue operation, with more than 250 first responders at the scene in Brooklyn, trying to find survivors who may have been trapped under the rubble of the three-storey building. Hours later, aerial video showed firefighters pulling a survivor, covered in dust, out of the debris on a stretcher. Authorities are yet to determine what caused the sudden collapse at about 16:00 local time (21:00 GMT) on Wednesday. The rescue mission has been described as "extremely dangerous" by New York City Fire Department (FDNY) Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore. She added that people from the collapsed building and also the construction site had been trapped. "Members have been working methodically and haven't stopped since they arrived this afternoon," Bonsignore said. Some pictures of the collapsed building, on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn, show an entire side of it gone, with bedrooms and closets exposed. Among the debris, smashed concrete and twisted metal, are household items and clothes. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani joined emergency responders at the scene, praising them for their rapid response. They "arrived in under a minute and have spent hours working in dangerous and highly technical conditions to rescue New Yorkers," he later wrote on X. The Brooklyn building was built in 1930, city records show, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. Related topics - Published2 hours ago

items.title: Merkez Bankası'ndan 200 baz puan faiz indirimi beklentisi: ING'den çarpıcı rapor
items.summary: ING, Türkiye'nin para politikasına ilişkin faiz beklentilerini paylaştı. Merkez Bankası'nın önümüzdeki dönemde atabileceği adımları değerlendiren kurum, 2026'da 200 baz puan, 2027 sonuna uzanan zaman diliminde ise toplam 700 baz puan indirim bekliyor.

items.summaryTr: ING, Türkiye'nin para politikasına ilişkin faiz beklentilerini paylaştı. Merkez Bankası'nın önümüzdeki dönemde atabileceği adımları değerlendiren kurum, 2026'da 200 baz puan, 2027 sonuna uzanan zaman diliminde ise toplam 700 baz puan indirim bekliyor.
items.articleText: Merkez Bankası'ndan 200 baz puan faiz indirimi beklentisi: ING'den çarpıcı rapor ING, Türkiye'nin para politikasına ilişkin faiz beklentilerini paylaştı. Merkez Bankası'nın önümüzdeki dönemde atabileceği adımları değerlendiren kurum, 2026'da 200 baz puan, 2027 sonuna uzanan zaman diliminde ise toplam 700 baz puan indirim bekliyor. Yüzde 30 faiz beklentisi ING, ekim ayında beklentilerin üzerinde gerçekleşen enflasyonun Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasının (TCMB) faiz indirim sürecini değiştirmesini beklemiyor. Banka, politika faizinin aralık ayında yüzde 37'den yüzde 35'e indirilmesini, 2027 yılı sonunda ise yüzde 30'a gerilemesini öngörüyor. ING ekonomistleri Muhammet Mercan, Frantisek Taborsky ve James Wilson tarafından hazırlanan "Monitoring Turkey" raporunda, ekim enflasyonunun son dönemdeki dezenflasyon eğilimini kesintiye uğrattığı ancak para politikasının genel görünümünü değiştirecek ölçüde olmadığı belirtildi. Aralık ayında 200 baz puanlık indirim beklentisi ING ekonomistleri, TCMB'nin son Para Politikası Kurulu (PPK) toplantısında politika yönlendirmesini değiştirdiğine dikkat çekti. Raporda, Merkez Bankasının önceki toplantı bazlı temkinli yaklaşım yerine, gelecekteki politika adımlarının zamanlamasına ve büyüklüğüne daha fazla vurgu yaptığı ifade edildi. Ekonomistler, temel ekonomik koşullarda önemli bir değişiklik yaşanmaması halinde faiz indirim döngüsünün aralık ayında devam etmesinin muhtemel olduğunu belirtti. ING, politika faizinin 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğindeki yüzde 37 seviyesinden yıl sonunda yüzde 35'e düşmesini bekliyor. 2027 sonunda yüzde 30 faiz tahmini ING'nin tahminlerine göre TCMB, faiz indirimlerini 2027 yılında da sürdürecek. Banka, politika faizinin 2027'nin ilk çeyreğinde yüzde 33'e, ikinci çeyreğinde yüzde 31'e, üçüncü çeyreğinde yüzde 30'a gerilemesini ve yılın son çeyreğinde yüzde 30 seviyesinde kalmasını öngörüyor. Jeopolitik riskler ve rezervler belirleyici olacak ING ekonomistleri, TCMB'nin para politikası açısından başlıca risklerin Orta Doğu'daki çatışmalar ve dezenflasyon sürecindeki olası değişimler olduğunu vurguladı. Raporda, petrol fiyatlarına ilişkin belirsizliklerin ve ABD-İran gerilimindeki kalıcı bir tırmanışın fiyat baskılarını hızla artırabileceği belirtildi. Ekonomistler 3 başlığı takip ediyor Ekonomistler, Merkez Bankasının gelecekteki faiz kararlarında talep koşullarını, uluslararası rezervleri ve mevduat sahiplerinin davranışlarını yakından izlemeye devam edeceğini ifade etti. ING, TCMB'nin 12 Kasım'da yayımlayacağı Enflasyon Raporu'nun enflasyonun seyri ve önümüzdeki dönemde para politikasında ilave gevşeme alanı konusunda yeni göstergeler sunabileceğini değerlendirdi.

items.summary: In a July interview, Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su explained how fake coding assessments could compromise employee devices, a tactic later used in the exchange’s record-breaking hack.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack
items.summaryTr: In a July interview, Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su explained how fake coding assessments could compromise employee devices, a tactic later used in the exchange’s record-breaking hack.
items.articleText: Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack In a July interview, Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su explained how fake coding assessments could compromise employee devices, a tactic later used in the exchange’s record-breaking hack. Months before Binance lost $6.3 billion to a hack, its chief security officer described to Cointelegraph how a fake job interview could give attackers a foothold inside the exchange — closely resembling one of the entry methods later used against the exchange. During a July interview about Binance’s response to rising security threats, Jimmy Su told Cointelegraph that fake job interviews were “something we worry about a lot internally,” explaining how attackers could tailor a job opportunity to an employee before persuading them to run code as part of a technical assessment. “And once that gets executed, the device is compromised and then they can start harvesting credentials,” Su said, adding that attackers could then use that to penetrate further into the network. Su’s detailed warning about malicious coding assessments was not included in Cointelegraph’s July coverage, but takes on new significance following the biggest crypto exchange hack in history. In September, a Binance software engineer downloaded a malicious coding assignment onto his work computer during a fake job interview. That compromise became part of the multistage attack that culminated in October’s theft, according to Binance’s preliminary investigation. During the interview with Cointelegraph, Su had also anticipated why security tools might miss such a trap. A technical assessment could involve seemingly legitimate steps, such as downloading a code repository from GitHub, he explained in July. “Each step is actually legitimate on its own. So a lot of the anti-virus tools may not be able to detect it and flag it,” he said. Binance’s investigation subsequently described a similar detection failure, saying the assignment’s setup process executed malware that evaded its endpoint security tools through obfuscation and other evasion techniques. Binance said onus is on the company to detect attacks Su told Cointelegraph that it was Binance’s responsibility to contain the risk when employees pursued outside opportunities on work computers. “Of course employees can explore outside opportunities. What we do worry about is that they do so on the company device,” he said. If an employee fell for a fake interview, he added, “the onus is on us to detect it,” and to “stop the actual execution of that code.” Related: North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic Binance was already testing employees against fake recruiters. Su said its internal red team had been conducting monthly phishing simulations for three to four years, with remedial training for employees who failed. “In the beginning, the security hygiene left a lot to be desired. But after this amount of time, the company has improved significantly,” he said. Kevin Gibson of recruitment firm Proof of Search told Cointelegraph that the threat is also changing how some crypto employers assess prospective hires, with clients increasingly wanting to know whether candidates have been met in person. “A number of our clients are now asking us straight up whether we’ve met a candidate in person,” Gibson said, adding that candidates personally met by a third-party recruiter have an advantage. Employees, like in Binance’s case, can also become targets. “In crypto, a dodgy job offer or a ‘quick catch-up call’ can be the first step in a multimillion-dollar hit,” he said. Binance blocks a North Korean cyber threat every five days Binance said it blocked 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threats so far this year, which is roughly one attack every five days. Following October’s attack, Binance said it had tightened device controls, rebuilt affected wallet systems and internal AI tooling, strengthened access controls and revoked compromised credentials. items.articleTextTr: Binance CSO unwittingly foreshadowed $6.3B hack tactic months before attack In a July interview, Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su explained how fake coding assessments could compromise employee devices, a tactic later used in the exchange’s record-breaking hack. Months before Binance lost $6.3 billion to a hack, its chief security officer described to Cointelegraph how a fake job interview could give attackers a foothold inside the exchange — closely resembling one of the entry methods later used against the exchange. During a July interview about Binance’s response to rising security threats, Jimmy Su told Cointelegraph that fake job interviews were “something we worry about a lot internally,” explaining how attackers could tailor a job opportunity to an employee before persuading them to run code as part of a technical assessment. “And once that gets executed, the device is compromised and then they can start harvesting credentials,” Su said, adding that attackers could then use that to penetrate further into the network. Su’s detailed warning about malicious coding assessments was not included in Cointelegraph’s July coverage, but takes on new significance following the biggest crypto exchange hack in history. In September, a Binance software engineer downloaded a malicious coding assignment onto his work computer during a fake job interview. That compromise became part of the multistage attack that culminated in October’s theft, according to Binance’s preliminary investigation. During the interview with Cointelegraph, Su had also anticipated why security tools might miss such a trap. A technical assessment could involve seemingly legitimate steps, such as downloading a code repository from GitHub, he explained in July. “Each step is actually legitimate on its own. So a lot of the anti-virus tools may not be able to detect it and flag it,” he said. Binance’s investigation subsequently described a similar detection failure, saying the assignment’s setup process executed malware that evaded its endpoint security tools through obfuscation and other evasion techniques. Binance said onus is on the company to detect attacks Su told Cointelegraph that it was Binance’s responsibility to contain the risk when employees pursued outside opportunities on work computers. “Of course employees can explore outside opportunities. What we do worry about is that they do so on the company device,” he said. If an employee fell for a fake interview, he added, “the onus is on us to detect it,” and to “stop the actual execution of that code.” Related: North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic Binance was already testing employees against fake recruiters. Su said its internal red team had been conducting monthly phishing simulations for three to four years, with remedial training for employees who failed. “In the beginning, the security hygiene left a lot to be desired. But after this amount of time, the company has improved significantly,” he said. Kevin Gibson of recruitment firm Proof of Search told Cointelegraph that the threat is also changing how some crypto employers assess prospective hires, with clients increasingly wanting to know whether candidates have been met in person. “A number of our clients are now asking us straight up whether we’ve met a candidate in person,” Gibson said, adding that candidates personally met by a third-party recruiter have an advantage. Employees, like in Binance’s case, can also become targets. “In crypto, a dodgy job offer or a ‘quick catch-up call’ can be the first step in a multimillion-dollar hit,” he said. items.articleText: Israeli strike on hospital kills at least five Palestinians, Gaza civil defence agency says - Published At least five Palestinians have been killed after an Israeli airstrike hit a building at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, an official from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency has told the BBC. Eyewitnesses said that a single missile, fired from a warplane that briefly flew over the area, struck a building housing the hospital's surgical wards and intensive care units. Twenty others were injured, the civil defence spokesman said. A surgeon is reported to be among those who were killed during the strike early on Thursday. There has been no immediate response from the Israeli military. The BBC has contacted the Israel Defense Forces for comment. Earlier, civil defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal told news agency AFP that six people had been killed. The BBC is prevented by Israel from reporting independently from inside the Gaza Strip, and is unable to verify details of the incident. Recovery work is carried out by the Civil Defence in Gaza, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry. Its efforts have been supported by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). Videos shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by the blast. Local activists circulated claims that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building. Israel often accuses Hamas, which continues to retain its weapons and maintain security control over the Gaza Strip, of using hospitals for military purposes. Hamas denies the allegations. Speaking to reporters in the aftermath of the strike, the director of Nasser Medical Complex said the building had been hit in a vertical strike, causing extensive damage to the intensive care and surgical departments for both men and women. Nasser Hospital, the largest in southern Gaza, was hit by a double Israeli strike in August 2025, which killed at least 20 people, including journalists and health workers. Israeli strikes on Gaza have continued despite a ceasefire agreement in October last year. More than 1,600 people have been killed since then, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire. The humanitarian crisis in Gaza has also worsened from recent heavy rains that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents that were housing displaced families. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Since then, more than 74,645 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.
